name: Example: Computing the Value of a Function of a Jordan Decomposition
problem:
Consider the following matrices:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072904/assets/17b4d68be43e4a4eb895ebbe623b713f1a808153424dd221b7497579d666b00a.png)

Given that $V = PJP^{-1},$ find $\sin\left(\pi V\right).$
worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and matrices $A$ and $S,$ where $S$ is invertible, we have

$$
f(SAS^{-1}) = S \cdot f(A) \cdot S^{-1}.
$$

For $f(x) = \sin(\pi x)$ and the given matrix $V,$ we have

$$
\sin(\pi V) = \sin\left(\pi{PJP^{-1}}\right) = P \cdot (\sin(\pi J)) \cdot P^{-1}.
$$

Now, since $J$ is a Jordan block with $-3$s on the main diagonal, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072904/assets/a8ad3d4a15a5a8e7307fdd6449d8086d6c9c7e656caea877d41f021c7d8584cc.png)

The derivative of $f$ is $f'(x) = \pi \cos \pi x.$ So, we get

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072904/assets/9af57a3b00b9c9e64508c119ae77690904bdb8c30b124b8165d4280149361bad.png)

Also, the inverse of $P$ is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072904/assets/ff9333784a9cdd38f510398b48e485764eac400f56c2cc9f2f1a18e5138845d8.png)

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi V) & =P\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi J))\cdot {P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -\pi  \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\pi  & -\pi  \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\pi  & -\pi  \\ \pi  & -\pi \end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
